candidates.snippet: Zoroaster was already famous in classical antiquity as the founder of the widely renowned wisdom of the Magi. His Evidence for his life. name is not mentioned by Herodotus in his sketch of the Medo-Persian religion (i. 131 seq.). It occurs for the first time in a fragment of Xanthus (29), and in the Alcibiades of Plato (i. p. 122), who calls him the son of Oromazdes. For occidental writers, Zoroaster is always the Magus , or the founder of the whole Magian system (Plut. de Is. et Osir. 46; Plat. loc. cit. ; Diog. Laërt. prooem. 2: other passages in Jackson's Zoroaster , 6 seq.). They sometimes call him a Bactrian, sometimes a Median or Persian (cf. Jackson, op. cit. 186).
